external_entities.name: sensor node
external_entities.description: A deployed sensor node installed on a customer site that publishes readings and polls for firmware updates.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Each node publishes readings over MQTT to the device gateway
external_entities.notes: The nodes are outside our physical control. The authentication key is per fleet, not per device.

external_entities.name: field technician
external_entities.description: A technician who services sensor nodes over a local serial console.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Field technicians service nodes over a local serial console.

external_entities.name: fleet operator
external_entities.description: An operator who views dashboards over BigQuery from the corporate network.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Our own fleet operators look at dashboards over BigQuery from the corporate network

processes.name: device gateway
processes.description: An MQTT broker running on GKE that accepts readings from sensor nodes and forwards them to Pub/Sub.
processes.source_excerpt: the device gateway, which is an MQTT broker we run on GKE
processes.notes: The gateway is exposed to the internet. Nodes authenticate to it with a fleet-wide pre-shared key that nobody has rotated since deployment.

processes.name: telemetry normalizer
processes.description: A Python consumer in the analytics network that picks up readings and writes them into the telemetry lake.
processes.source_excerpt: the telemetry normalizer, a Python consumer in our analytics network

data_stores.name: device registry
data_stores.description: A Firestore registry used by the gateway to check a device key and determine which customer a node belongs to.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The gateway looks up the device in a device registry (Firestore) to check the key

data_stores.name: Pub/Sub
data_stores.description: A Pub/Sub queue onto which the gateway forwards accepted readings for the telemetry normalizer.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Readings the gateway accepts are forwarded onto Pub/Sub

data_stores.name: telemetry lake
data_stores.description: A BigQuery data store containing telemetry, site addresses, and occupancy patterns.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The lake has site addresses and occupancy patterns in it, so it is customer data.

data_stores.name: Cloud Storage bucket
data_stores.description: A bucket from which sensor nodes poll for new firmware images.
data_stores.source_excerpt: nodes poll a Cloud Storage bucket for a new image
data_stores.notes: The bucket is public read. The source does not establish whether nodes check a signature before installing an image.

data_flows.name: publish readings
data_flows.source_excerpt: Each node publishes readings over MQTT to the device gateway

data_flows.name: look up device
data_flows.source_excerpt: The gateway looks up the device in a device registry (Firestore) to check the key and to find out which customer the node belongs to.
data_flows.data_description: device identity, authentication key, and customer association

data_flows.name: forward readings
data_flows.source_excerpt: Readings the gateway accepts are forwarded onto Pub/Sub

data_flows.name: pick up readings
data_flows.source_excerpt: picked up by the telemetry normalizer

data_flows.name: write readings
data_flows.source_excerpt: which writes them into the telemetry lake in BigQuery
data_flows.data_description: sensor readings, including site addresses and occupancy patterns

data_flows.name: poll image
data_flows.source_excerpt: nodes poll a Cloud Storage bucket for a new image
data_flows.notes: The bucket is public read, so the source does not state that nodes authenticate to it. I do not know whether the nodes check a signature on the image before installing it.

data_flows.name: service console
data_flows.source_excerpt: Field technicians service nodes over a local serial console.
data_flows.notes: I don't know what authentication that console has, if any.

data_flows.name: view dashboards
data_flows.source_excerpt: Our own fleet operators look at dashboards over BigQuery from the corporate network, signed in with company SSO.

trust_boundaries.name: customer site

trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: sensor nodes installed on customer sites

trust_boundaries.description: The analytics network in which the telemetry normalizer runs.

assumptions.basis: The source describes readings from customer-site devices and identifies the resulting lake contents as customer data.

assumptions.basis: The gateway checks the key and accepts readings.

assumptions.basis: The normalizer picks up readings and writes them to the lake containing customer data.

assumptions.assumption: The device registry carries credentials because it stores or provides the key used for authentication.
assumptions.basis: The gateway looks up the device in the registry to check the key.

assumptions.assumption: Pub/Sub carries personal data because the gateway forwards accepted readings onto it.
assumptions.basis: The source states that accepted readings are forwarded onto Pub/Sub.

assumptions.assumption: The telemetry lake carries personal data because it contains site addresses and occupancy patterns.
assumptions.basis: The source explicitly identifies those contents as customer data.
